note: Data for electron/setup-plan.cjs chatModelFor. Tags, download sizes, context, capabilities and licence were read from ollama.com; the memory a tag needs (download size x 1.2, or the row's own weightsMargin) and every speed statement are FRIDAY estimates and stay unverified until the owner's PC runs them. A tag is never chosen unless its weights plus that margin fit the usable memory. The tier is chosen from the TOTAL memory of the PC (free memory only warns), so an open browser never changes the planned model.

rules.cpuReserveNote: Memory Windows, Electron and speech keep, by the PC's total RAM: 2 GB at 4 GB, 4.5 GB at 8 GB, 6 GB from 16 GB, linear in between; below 4 GB it stays 2 GB, so a PC with 3 GB or less gets no local chat model.
rules.ollamaGpuRuleSource: https://docs.ollama.com/gpu read 2026-11-28: NVIDIA compute capability 5.0 and newer with driver 550 and newer; compute capability 5.0 to 6.2 needs driver 570 and newer
rules.vulkanNote: A dedicated AMD or Intel card with at least 6 GB of video memory (not an integrated part, not a unified-memory APU) runs the chat model through Ollama's Vulkan backend (https://docs.ollama.com/gpu read 2026-11-28: 'Additional GPU support on Windows and Linux is provided via Vulkan'). Speed is estimated, not measured.

noAvx2.note: no AVX2 on the processor: llama.cpp uses its plain CPU build, so the chat model is capped at 2b (0.8b on a weak processor)

arm64.note: x64 emulation, slow: ARM64 Windows runs the x64 build by emulation, so the chat model is capped at 2b (0.8b on a weak processor)
arm64.nativeNote: native ARM64 llama.cpp build: the chat model is capped at 4b (0.8b on a weak processor) until its speed is measured on this PC

numCtx.note: num_ctx is the largest ladder step that fits half the memory left after the weights and after a row's fixed `kvFixedGb` (the sliding-window layers' cache, which does not grow with the window), within the model's native context and the device cap; a PC under 6 GB of RAM gets 2k and under 9 GB 4k, as kernel/router.py does. kvKbPerToken is the f16 key-value cache of one token: full-attention layers x 2 x key-value heads x head size x 2 bytes, from the model cards.

ollamaSettings.note: Applied by FRIDAY when it starts or calls Ollama, never forced on the owner's own Ollama setup. Ollama's default context is 4096. q8_0 KV cache only pays off at 16k context and more. Flash attention is left to Ollama (unset = automatic): https://docs.ollama.com/faq read 2026-11-28 says OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION accepts 1 (force on) or 0 (off), so the word 'automatic' is never written to that variable.

qualityFamilies.note: Ranking heuristic to decide whether a model already installed is at least as good as the tier choice: parameter count (MoE: geometric mean of total and active) times the family factor. Not a benchmark.
